coins.name: RAKBank AED Stablecoin
coins.launchPhaseDetail: RAKBank (The National Bank of Ras Al Khaimah P.S.C.) received in-principle approval from the Central Bank of the UAE on January 7 2026 to issue an AED-backed payment token (stablecoin), subject to completion of regulatory and operational requirements under the CBUAE Payment Token Services Regulation. Planned to be fully backed 1:1 by dirhams in segregated, regulated accounts with full redemption at par, audited smart contracts, and real-time reserve attestations, targeting digital payments, asset tokenization, and cross-border settlements. The first conventional commercial-bank AED payment token under the CBUAE regime, distinct from Zand AED, AE Coin (Al Maryah), and the FAB/ADQ/IHC dirham initiative. Ticker, chains, issuing-entity structure, and launch timing not yet announced; a pilot phase will follow in due course. Pharos tracks the AED peg as OTHER until dirham peg support is built.

milestones.title: CBUAE grants RAKBank in-principle approval to issue an AED-backed stablecoin

coins.name: ARC
coins.launchPhaseDetail: India's first regulated rupee stablecoin; built by Anq with Polygon; 1:1 INR collateralized by cash, fixed deposits, and government securities; designed to prevent USD liquidity outflow; two-tier framework complementing RBI's CBDC; Uniswap v4 whitelisting for compliance. The tentative January 2026 debut has passed with no RBI confirmation, no live circulating supply, and no ARC mention on anq.finance. Its status was uncertain as of mid-2026. In July 2026 the RBI signaled to a Parliamentary Standing Committee that it favors barring banks and regulated entities from exposure to private stablecoins, including rupee-backed ones, putting the project's regulated-INR-stablecoin premise in question. As of September 13 2026 anq.finance still carries no ARC mention; the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance rescheduled its Department of Economic Affairs evidence session on virtual digital assets to September 16 2026. No source supports a 2026 launch, so Pharos removed the expectation on September 13 2026

milestones.title: ARC rupee stablecoin announced by Anq and Polygon

coins.name: BILS
coins.launchPhaseDetail: Bits of Gold, a Tel Aviv-based licensed crypto broker/custodian operating since 2013, received full regulatory approval on April 28 2026 from Israel's Capital Market, Insurance and Savings Authority (CMISA) to issue BILS, the first regulated shekel-pegged stablecoin, following a two-year sandbox pilot approved in March 2024. Backed 1:1 by New Israeli Shekels held in segregated dedicated bank accounts within Israel (foreign custody excluded), audited by Ernst & Young, with Fireblocks custody/issuance infrastructure and QEDIT zero-knowledge privacy, issued on Solana via token extensions. The regulator mandates a deliberately gradual, small-scale rollout (likely institutional/qualified participants first) before wide availability; no firm public-launch date set. As of September 27 2026 the Solana mint (CDxFUPSRK4dC68jWV7SCPezU1vNYXz87Y6fjhhRvsuhd) still holds a flat 100,000 BILS with no mint activity since August 6 2026, while the bils.co.il transparency page states 1.1M BILS in circulation, a figure the published Solana contract does not support; the site also describes issuance on Solana and Ethereum but publishes no Ethereum address. On August 16 2026 Bits of Gold disclosed a breach of up to 250,000 customers' personal details through a third-party analytics provider, reporting it to CMISA with funds unaffected. The transparency page lists the EY Q3 2026 report as pending, and the white paper served as new in September 2026 is internally dated June 2025. CoinGecko carries the mint with no price or tickers. Distinct from Israel's broader Stablecoin Law, which remains in draft/public-comment stage. Pharos tracks the ILS peg as OTHER until shekel peg support is built.

coins.name: B3 BRL Stablecoin
coins.launchPhaseDetail: Latin America's largest stock exchange (B3/Sao Paulo) is developing B3RL, its own BRL settlement stablecoin for tokenized-asset trading. At B3's Tokenization Day (May 26-27 2026), coverage indicated a later-2026 / H2 2026 window for B3RL and the tokenized-asset registry; the prior H1 2026 window elapsed with no on-chain deployment visible. At Expert XP on July 23-24 2026 B3 placed the launch between August and September 2026, and its Q2 2026 results note (August 11) confirmed infrastructure testing of B3RL had begun, the first B3-owned confirmation of the ticker. That window also lapsed: at B3 Week on September 15 2026 digital-assets director Felipe Paiva said infrastructure for new use cases, including tokenized collateral, would be ready at the start of 2027, and September reporting frames B3RL as a 2027 launch. Backing is mainly cash and Tesouro Nacional securities, with Polygon named in Brazilian press and by Paiva. No deployment was visible as of September 27 2026, and Pharos moved the expected launch to 2027 on September 27 2026. On October 8 2026 B3 said B3RL will not settle the first tokenized shares targeted for early 2027 and that the settlement currency remains undecided. Pharos moved the launch phase from launching-soon to testnet on October 18 2026, reflecting infrastructure testing with no near-term settlement role.

coins.name: Itau Unibanco BRL Stablecoin
coins.launchPhaseDetail: Itau Unibanco (Brazil's largest private bank by assets, ~5.6T BRL) is evaluating its own stablecoin. Head of Digital Assets Guto Antunes confirmed exploration at an industry event in Sao Paulo in April 2025: 'we are always open to understanding whether it makes sense for our clients to have a stablecoin, even one in real, within Itau'. Brazil's virtual-asset framework (Consultas Publicas 109-111) was finalised as BCB Resolutions 519, 520, and 521 in November 2025 and took effect on February 2 2026; peg-currency choice (BRL or USD) and product timeline remain undisclosed. Itau already participates in the DREX wholesale CBDC pilot, providing distribution-rail experience; ticker not yet announced. Pharos tracks BRL as the most likely first launch given the Brazilian retail base, but the editorial summary documents the open USD option. In May 2026, BCB Resolution 561 (effective Oct 1 2026) banned authorised FX providers from using stablecoins or crypto to settle cross-border remittances, tightening the regulatory backdrop. At Blockchain.RIO on August 13 2026 Antunes said stablecoins and tokenised deposits must coexist, without committing to an Itau-issued token. No source has given a launch timeline since the April 2025 remark, so Pharos removed the 2026 expectation on September 13 2026.

Aimed at B2B payments, remittances, and settlement. Reserve composition not yet disclosed.

coins.name: Revolut Euro
coins.launchPhaseDetail: EURR is live, not forthcoming. Pharos tracks it pre-launch only because it is not yet admissible to runtime data. Revolut launched the token on August 26 2026 as the first product of its stablecoin programme, in euro rather than the dollar or sterling tokens it had been expected to ship first. The issuer of record is Bridge Building S.A., the Luxembourg entity of Stripe-owned Bridge, holding an EMI licence and MiCA authorisation from the CSSF; Revolut Digital Assets Europe Ltd distributes the token under its own CySEC MiCA licence. This is a third-party issuer relationship, not in-house issuance from Revolut's Lithuanian EMI as earlier reporting had assumed. The token is an ERC-20 at 0x8e9c32a536ab623a2e0e9961bce6f5fe7504e084 on Ethereum (6 decimals, name "Revolut Euro"), with a second deployment on Polygon at 0x11b20f798b70df2201D8F550ADDcc3378b33dd4A holding 3 EURR, and Solana, Arbitrum, Optimism, Avalanche, Injective, TON, and Sui listed as intended networks in the MiCA white paper. That white paper set the public offer start at August 20 2026, six days before the app rollout. Rollout is phased, reaching Denmark, Poland, and Portugal first with wider EEA availability targeted later in 2026, and Revolut charges no spread or fee on euro-to-EURR conversion. Supply grew from 366 EURR to 250,957 EURR in the first two days, held flat through August 31, then rose again through the first week of September to 1,671,782.16 EURR (about $1.94M) on September 6 2026, and has since moved less than 2,000 EURR: 1,674,912.63 on September 12 and 1,676,863.60 on September 27. DefiLlama began tracking EURR as stablecoin id 436 on August 27 2026 and now carries that supply, but its price field is null. CoinGecko's revolut-euro has since picked up the Ethereum contract mapping and the matching total supply, yet it remains a preview listing returning no price and no market cap, /simple/price returns an empty object, and coins.llama.fi resolves neither the contract nor the CoinGecko id. Supply is measurable; no accepted source returns a fetchable price, so Pharos holds EURR pre-launch until a price path exists. Bridge's reserve page (reserves.bridge.xyz/eurr, updated September 27 2026) reports 1,676,867 EURR outstanding against EUR 1,676,867 of reserves held entirely as cash deposits at credit institutions; custodian names and an independent attestation remain unpublished.

coins.name: Tether Georgian Lari Stablecoin
coins.launchPhaseDetail: Announced May 25 2026 as a joint Tether / Government of Georgia initiative to place the Georgian Lari on digital-asset rails; not a CBDC (distinct from the NBG's separate digital-lari pilot). Tether signed an MOU with Georgia in June 2023 and has invested in CityPay.io (active at 2,000+ Georgian merchant locations); GEL₮ is stated to be issued on multiple blockchains. coins.name: HKDAP
coins.launchPhaseDetail: HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuer FRS01, effective April 10 2026; JV between Standard Chartered, HKT, and Animoca Brands; 1:1 backed by HKD-denominated high-quality liquid assets. On May 13 2026, Anchorpoint, OSL Group, and PantherTrade completed a full-lifecycle test transfer on Ethereum mainnet (fiat funding, reserve, mint, transfer, full redemption) without putting tokens into circulation, confirming Ethereum as the deployment chain. The original end-of-Q2 2026 phased rollout target closed on June 30, 2026 with no public circulating token. On July 21 2026 Caixin reported, citing people familiar with the plans, that Anchorpoint will launch HKDAP within the month with distribution through licensed exchanges OSL and HashKey, which are already testing payment and fund use cases. The July window then closed without a launch: on August 3 2026 Standard Chartered CEO (HK) Mary Huen said work continues since the April licence, public-blockchain testing is ongoing, and the HKDAP launch announcement is now expected within August 2026, with a B2B2C distributor model whose distributor list follows the formal launch. The August window was met: on August 11 2026 OSL Group announced it was among the first key authorised distributors under an HKDAP beta access programme, and on August 12 2026 HashKey Exchange joined as a distributor and reported completing an initial mint-and-redemption cycle including fiat conversion both ways. Access is restricted to institutions, corporate clients, and professional investors, with retail targeted no earlier than late 2026. Anchorpoint has published no launch press release of its own. The anchorpoint.hk site still reads 'has not yet officially launched' with an empty partner list, so the go-live is sourced from the distributors. Anchorpoint disclosed neither the first-transaction value nor the admitted client count, but the deployment is now identified: HKDAP is an upgradeable ERC-20 at 0x87622385F960fcCB3121d6D0A9513bd1D9Bed6cA on Ethereum (6 decimals, name "HKD At Par"), carrying a supply of 527,199.52 HKDAP as of August 29 2026, which held flat through August 31 and then rose across the first week of September to 698,833.91 HKDAP (about $89.1K) on September 6 2026 and 875,549.91 HKDAP (about $111.6K) on September 12 2026, then 1,006,889.91 HKDAP (about $128.3K) on September 20 2026, flat since September 18. On September 14 2026 Payment Asia Group reported the first named commercial use: a full fund-mint-pay-reconcile-redeem-burn cycle with OSL as distributor, settling ShipAny logistics fees and Flow hospitality employee benefits, without disclosed amounts. Standard Chartered became the first bank distributor on August 24 2026, with Finloop, Yunfeng Financial, and a Bank of East Asia memorandum following on August 25-28, and on September 15 2026 Anchorpoint launched the Tokenised Money Adoption Programme with PwC Hong Kong as inaugural strategic partner. Supply reached 1,006,889.91 HKDAP (about $128.3K) on September 27 2026, roughly double August 27, with ten holder addresses and no remediation of the BlockSec findings announced. On August 14 2026 BlockSec published a contract review reporting that the KYC proof argument is discarded so any proof passes, that de-registering a compromised KYC provider does not stop wallets it onboarded, that a single key can mint, burn, pause, or freeze while two keys control all upgrades and roles, and that debug logging, a zero-run optimizer, and uploaded test files suggest a pre-production build was deployed to mainnet. DefiLlama began tracking HKDAP as stablecoin id 437 on August 27 2026, reporting circulating supply consistent with the on-chain figure. Supply is therefore now measurable, but no accepted source returns a price: the DefiLlama list price field is null, coins.llama.fi resolves neither the Ethereum contract nor the CoinGecko id, and anchorpoint-hkd-at-par remains a preview listing with zero supply and no platforms. Pharos holds HKDAP pre-launch until a fetchable price path exists.

coins.name: Japan Megabank JPY Stablecoin
coins.launchPhaseDetail: Announced June 10 2026 by MUFG Bank, Mizuho Bank, and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, Japan's three largest banks, which entered a memorandum of understanding to establish a voluntary council for jointly examining operational frameworks, governance, and related matters toward a jointly issued stablecoin. The Three Banks aim to conduct actual commercial transactions during fiscal year 2026 (ending March 2027) using a stablecoin issued pursuant to a trust agreement under which they act as joint settlors and a trust bank or similar institution acts as trustee; the production trustee is not yet named. The council examines issuance infrastructure, system and scheme design, and governance, and will consider collaboration with other financial institutions that may participate in the future. The initiative builds on a demonstration experiment selected in November 2025 as a supported project under the Financial Services Agency's FinTech Proof-of-Concept Hub, part of the joint exploration the three banks have conducted since 2024 under the Project Pax lineage. Nikkei reporting on June 9 2026 described a yen-denominated token issued on MUFG's Progmat platform with a US dollar version to follow and a one trillion yen business-to-business volume target by 2028; the banks' own release names neither denomination nor platform. On October 16 2026 the banks reported a July 17 to 23 trial of the jointly issued model with Mitsubishi UFJ Trust and Banking as trustee, trust assets held in bank deposits, no issuance cap, and circulation limited to bank-verified users; the release calls the design provisional. No ticker, production chain, production trustee, reserve composition, or attestation arrangement has been announced.

coins.name: JPYdf
coins.launchPhaseDetail: JPY DeFi launched on Ethereum mainnet on October 15 2026, so JPYdf is live. Pharos tracks it pre-launch only because no runtime price source admits it: on launch day DefiLlama and CoinGecko listed neither the token nor the protocol, and the DefiLlama contract-price endpoint returned no quote. The token is 0xb122f4a154f84708407213d6a715181180012f45 (18 decimals, Ethereum only, no registered bridge minter). At block 26196851 (08:54 UTC on October 15), supply was 91,738,933 JPYdf, about $581,000 at that day's yen rate, with 69.4 million borrowed against USDC and 22.3 million against wstETH. Trading was confined to one Uniswap v4 JPYdf/USDC pool created that morning with about $552,000 of liquidity. The token and the Liquity v2 core are non-upgradeable and the token owner is renounced. The dToken vault and strategy layer is upgradeable and pausable, and governance can recognize collateral losses, replace oracle sources after a 12-hour timelock and resume paused branches without delay. The governance, operator and guardian Safes are each 2-of-3 with the same three signers, although the documentation describes a higher quorum for loss recognition. The deployed JPY/USD staleness threshold is 30 hours, while the documentation describes 72 hours. Chain Defenders and Guardian reviewed the JPYdf-specific code; the bug bounty and confidential disclosure channel were not active at launch. JPYdf Foundation DAO LLC operates the app, which excludes Japanese residents, and does not disclose its domicile.

coins.name: Revolut GBP Stablecoin
coins.launchPhaseDetail: Selected as one of four firms for FCA Regulatory Sandbox stablecoin cohort (Feb 25); testing began Q1 2026; full UK banking licence granted Mar 11, but GBP stablecoin would be issued from Revolut Ltd (e-money entity), not Revolut Bank UK, per BoE proposed rule on subsidiary issuance; Head of UK Policy Rory Tanner outlined proposition to House of Lords (Mar 25), flagging UK→India remittance corridor as priority use case; ticker not publicly confirmed; the Bank of England softened its stance in May 2026, dropping the £20k individual holding cap in favour of aggregate issuer caps (revised draft rules due June 2026) and signalling banks may issue branded coins via ring-fenced subsidiaries, though the 40% unremunerated-reserve requirement remains under review. On June 2 2026 the House of Lords Financial Services Regulation Committee urged the BoE to scrap individual holding limits entirely and reconsider that 40% floor. On June 22 2026 the BoE published its final policy statement and draft rules: individual holding limits are scrapped in favour of a temporary per-coin issuance cap (initially ~£40bn / $50bn), the short-dated-UK-T-bill reserve share rises to 70% with the remainder held at the BoE and no yield paid to holders, and par redemption within 24 hours is required; a Code of Practice consultation runs to September 22 2026, with rules finalised by end-2026 and regulated sterling stablecoins operating from 2027. On August 26 2026 Revolut shipped the first token of its stablecoin programme: the euro-denominated EURR, on Ethereum, issued by Bridge Building S.A. (Stripe's Bridge) under MiCA rather than by a Revolut entity. That establishes Revolut's working issuance template as a third-party regulated issuer relationship, though it carries no direct read-through to sterling: EURR could ship because MiCA is in force, whereas RGBP remains blocked on a UK regime whose Code of Practice consultation runs to September 22 2026 and whose rules are not finalised until end-2026. The June 30 2026 BoE/FCA joint approach sets the FCA regime start at October 25 2027, with systemic issuers transferring to BoE prudential oversight on HM Treasury recognition.

coins.launchPhaseDetail: Companion to the already-tracked RGBP (Revolut GBP). Revolut secured a MiCA CASP licence from Cyprus (CySEC) on Oct 23 2025 and operates an existing EMI licence in Lithuania, the legal foundations for issuing e-money tokens under MiCA Title IV. In October 2025, Revolut launched fee-free 1:1 USD↔stablecoin swaps (USDC/USDT on Ethereum, Solana, and Tron) for its 65M users; stablecoin payment volumes on the platform surged 156% in 2025 to ~$10.5B. In February 2026, the FCA selected Revolut as one of 4 firms (from 20 applicants) for a UK stablecoin payment testing pilot, though that sandbox is specifically for a GBP token, not USD. Revolut received a full UK banking licence from the PRA (Mar 11 2026) and filed an OCC national bank charter application for Revolut Bank US, N.A. (Mar 5 2026, targeting a 2027 US launch with built-in stablecoin access). Revolut's stablecoin programme shipped on August 26 2026, but in euro rather than dollars. EURR launched on Ethereum in a phased rollout to Denmark, Poland, and Portugal, with Solana, Arbitrum, Optimism, Avalanche, Injective, TON, and Sui support planned, alongside the removal of Tether's USDt from Revolut's European retail offering by August 31 2026. Critically, EURR is issued by Bridge Building S.A., the Luxembourg entity of Stripe-owned Bridge, with Revolut Digital Assets Europe authorised through CySEC. Revolut's Lithuanian EMI was not the issuer of record, contrary to earlier reporting. That correction matters for RUSD: the nearest live precedent for a Revolut dollar token is a third-party MiCA issuer relationship rather than in-house EMT issuance. On September 2 2026 the OCC granted preliminary conditional approval for Revolut Bank US, N.A. (Corporate Decision #1390), with opening targeted for the first half of 2027; the decision records that the bank plans to offer Revolut-branded stablecoins through a third-party issuer and will not manage reserves, matching the Bridge template used for EURR. A Revolut-branded USD stablecoin still has not been confirmed, and its ticker, chain selection, issuer entity, and reserve disclosure model all remain unannounced. Pharos moved the expected launch to 2027 on September 13 2026 on the strength of the OCC timeline.

coins.name: Flipcash USDF
coins.launchPhaseDetail: Debut token on Coinbase's Custom Stablecoin platform; went live 2026-05-20 on Solana, 1:1 backed by USDC, with Coinbase Onramp fiat access; serves as the settlement asset for Flipcash's user-created currencies; the on-chain reserve contract (github.com/code-payments/flipcash-program) was audited by Sec3. The Solana mint is 5AMAA9JV9H97YYVxx8F6FsCMmTwXSuTTQneiup4RYAUQ (6 decimals, pinned in the issuer's flipcash-program repository, created January 8 2026); it carried 2,875,649.80 USDF across 529 holders with no DEX pairs and no price on Jupiter on September 13 2026, and by September 27 2026 supply had grown to 3,181,003.29 USDF. USDF is not listed on DefiLlama or CoinGecko and Jupiter returns no market for the mint, so it cannot yet enter Pharos runtime data. As of July 2026 the token remains in Coinbase-exchange operational-only backend testing (no trading, deposits, or withdrawals) and the May 2026 public-launch window has lapsed without a confirmed go-live.

milestones.title: USDF launches as first Coinbase Custom Stablecoin
USDF goes live on Solana via Coinbase's Custom Stablecoin platform
USDF supply reaches 3.18 million on Solana with still no market, price feed, or trading launch

coins.name: VersaBank VUSD
coins.launchPhaseDetail: Internal USDVB pilot announced August 26, 2025, with limited designated external deposit-partner/client deployment planned. Pilot is not a supported catalog launch-phase enum, so no launchPhase is assigned. Commercial launch requires the bank’s stated OCC non-objection process; the September 1, 2026 filing still seeks regulatory confirmation of deposit-insurance eligibility and the ability to pay interest. On October 15 2026 VersaBank announced the US commercial phase, under which VersaBank USA is to issue a tokenized deposit branded VUSD; the release names no chain or date. Pharos tracks the commercial token as VUSD from October 15 2026; USDVB remains the pilot name. No current launch window or official chain-qualified asset addresses are established.

milestones.title: VersaBank USA launches internal USDVB pilot
Quarterly filing retains conditional tokenized-deposit strategy
VersaBank announces the US commercial phase of its tokenized deposits with VUSD

coins.name: USTX
coins.launchPhaseDetail: tx announced USTX on September 23, 2026 as a fully backed 1:1 stablecoin issued by Brale, native to tx, with an October 2026 launch window. No exact launch day, native asset address, decimals or token-specific control and redemption terms are established. tx is a planned ecosystem, not an authored supported deployment.

milestones.title: tx announces native USTX issued by Brale

coins.name: Aplauz WEUR
coins.launchPhaseDetail: The current whitepaper, amended 24 August 2026, states in Part G that WEUR has not yet launched or entered circulation. The homepage offers account creation, issuance and redemption and claims public on-chain verification, creating a lifecycle ambiguity without independently verified production contracts or circulation. Whitepaper publication and offer-start on 8 July are not confirmed issuance dates. ESMA records whitepaper notification on 25 June 2026, separately from its 26 May last-update field. No confirmed launch date is published.

milestones.title: ESMA records WEUR whitepaper notification
Whitepaper publication and offer-start date
Amended whitepaper states WEUR has not launched
